note: The unit here is the VOLUME, not the page. Every page of a declared volume was cropped, laid out and walked; the cards kept are the ones whose body names Chicago, Cook County or Illinois, and the rest are read and not kept. Declaring the pages would be a lie in the other direction — it would report a hole on every page that carries no Illinois family, and there are hundreds of them. A volume declared here is READ; what the reading is WORTH is the per-volume precision figure in precision_sample.json, and volume 4's is 0.475 against 0.975, 0.875 and 0.900. Coverage and quality are two different questions and this file only answers the first.

declarations.note: Volume 1 (A-C), Internet Archive file FL2091539_CP-130151_01.pdf, 987 pages, read by its text layer in four cropped column passes. 58,488 cards assembled; 2,579 kept for naming Chicago, Cook County or Illinois; 581 of those name Chicago or Cook County.

Volume 2 (C-H), Internet Archive file FL2091536_CP-130151_02.pdf, 1,016 pages, read by its text layer in the same four cropped column passes. 58,589 cards assembled; 1,987 kept for naming Chicago, Cook County or Illinois; 501 of those name Chicago or Cook County. Forty were drawn and adjudicated against the page image at 0.875 precision — 20 of 20 in the Chicago-and-Cook stratum, 15 of 20 in the Illinois-only one; the five bad keeps are two classes, and T-0600 carries the rules that would strike them. T-0601 carries the column-sliver double count the same draw found.

Volume 3 (H-P), Internet Archive file FL1982465_CP-130151_03.pdf, 1,003 pages, read by its text layer in the same four cropped column passes. 68,552 cards assembled; 2,131 kept for naming Chicago, Cook County or Illinois; 520 of those name Chicago or Cook County. Forty were drawn and adjudicated against the page image at 0.900 precision — 20 of 20 in the Chicago-and-Cook stratum, 16 of 20 in the Illinois-only one; the four bad keeps are one old class (the regnal Calendarium, through the rule written to stop it) and three new ones, all of them text that is not on the card: a neighbouring column's sliver, a genealogy's index VOLUME cited in roman ('See index III.'), and a stray mark at the start of a line. T-0600 carries the rules.

Volume 4 (P-Z), Internet Archive file 130151_04.pdf, 918 pages, read by its text layer in the same four cropped column passes. 6,548 cards assembled; 308 kept for naming Chicago, Cook County or Illinois; 10 of those name Chicago or Cook County. READ, AND THE READING IS POOR, AND THE POVERTY IS THE SOURCE'S: volumes 1-3 assembled 59, 58 and 68 cards a page and this one assembles 7, on pages that carry about 100. Forty were drawn and adjudicated against the page image at 0.475 precision — 9 of 10 in the Chicago-and-Cook stratum, which is this volume's whole population of it, and 10 of 30 in the Illinois-only one. The crop geometry was measured and ruled out as the cause; the file is the one volume in the Archive item without the Newberry's scan id. T-0613 carries the tesseract re-read that recovers the cards, and until it lands this volume's cards are not worth what volumes 1-3's are.
